hook: “AI writes your code?” stops the scroll.
“Learn how” gives it nowhere to go.
voice.lede: Semgrep’s webinar ad opens with the question AppSec teams are already asking. Then the promise goes soft: learn how to keep it secure, on a stock billboard, with no hint of what the session teaches. The page knows the better answer. It talks about real, reachable vulnerabilities without the noise, and that line never made it into the ad. The webinar ran on September 24 and the page now serves it on demand.

findings.title: A question that names the fear
findings.what: “AI writes your code?” is the exact anxiety this buyer has right now. It is short, direct and needs no category knowledge.

findings.title: “Learn how” says nothing specific
findings.what: “Learn how to keep it secure” could sit on any webinar. It never mentions noise, triage or reachable vulnerabilities, the things an AppSec team cares about.
findings.fix: Borrow the page’s own line: find reachable vulnerabilities in AI-generated code without drowning in noise.

findings.title: A billboard that could sell anything
findings.what: A lit billboard in a dark studio has nothing to do with code, AppSec or AI. The visual adds a frame and no meaning.
findings.fix: Show the problem: a pull request written by an agent with one reachable finding flagged.

findings.title: A date, a partner and no ask
findings.what: The creative gives the date and the BridgeIT partnership, then stops. There is no written next step, so the reader has to work out that this is a signup.
findings.fix: Put the action on the creative: save your seat, with the date beside it.

findings.title: Same session, same partner
findings.what: The title, the topic and BridgeIT all carry over, and the page names both speakers. The ad’s claim holds after the click.

findings.title: Three asks on one page
findings.what: “Book demo” and “Try for free” sit above the signup form, and the form’s own button just says “Submit.” The one action this page exists for has the weakest label.
findings.fix: Change “Submit” to “Watch the session” and let it be the loudest button on the page.

faq.q: What is wrong with Semgrep’s LinkedIn webinar ad?
faq.a: The hook works and the promise behind it does not. “AI writes your code?” earns attention, then “learn how to keep it secure” gives no specific reason to register.

faq.q: Why does a vague webinar promise hurt?
faq.a: A webinar asks for time as well as an email. The reader needs to know what they will leave with, and a topic alone does not tell them.

faq.q: Should a webinar page keep demo and trial buttons?
faq.a: They can stay in the navigation, but the signup has to be the strongest action on the page. If “Submit” is the quietest button, the page is arguing against itself.

issues.title: Headline Clarity
issues.explanation: 'AI writes your code? Learn how to keep it secure.' is a clear question-hook that names the exact anxiety this ICP has right now.

issues.title: CTA Friction
issues.explanation: No written CTA button text on the creative itself, just a date and partner name; viewer has to infer this is a sign-up ask.

issues.title: Visual-Copy Match
issues.explanation: Billboard-in-a-dark-studio visual is generic stock-concept, doesn't connect to code, AppSec, or the AI theme the copy raises.

issues.title: Benefit Specificity
issues.explanation: 'Learn how to keep it secure' is vague; no mention of false positives, triage burden, or specific tooling pain this ICP actually has.

issues.title: Trust Signals
issues.explanation: BridgeIT co-host adds some credibility but there's no speaker name, title, or proof point suggesting why this webinar is worth 45 minutes.
